title: Routing-header divergence: Rust enforces RPL SRH type-3 + checksum over final destination, Python accepts any Routing type and checksums over outer destination
description: Confirmed empirically by 2 independent codereview passes (discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-xuc8). Rust validate_full_ipv6 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:297-317) requires Routing type 3 (RPL RH3), rejects ext_len<24/flags!=0/segments_left>address_count, and when segments_left==0 verifies the UDP checksum over the FINAL destination per RFC 2460 s8.1 (codec.rs:314-316,345). Python validate_full_ipv6 (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:125-133 + python/src/lichen/ipv6/packet.py:237-248) walks ANY Routing header via generic TLV with no type/segments validation and always checksums over the outer destination. Diverges in BOTH directions with concrete trigger bytes: (A) valid RH3+UDP checksummed over final dst -> Rust Rule255 Ok, Python fatal 'invalid Rule 255 IPv6 UDP checksum' (Rust-encoded in-transit datagram fatally rejected by Python); (B) Routing type 0 (forbidden class, RFC 5095) with segments_left=1 and outer-dst checksum -> Python Rule255 accepted and forwarded, Rust fatal 'unsupported RPL source-routing header'. Same wire bytes get opposite verdicts on both encode and decode. Fix needs one canonical policy (RH3-only + RFC 2460 s8.1 checksum scope is the standards-correct candidate), aligned Python+Rust, plus shared SRH fallback/malformed vectors. Related but distinct: project-LICHEN-worker6-prld (Rule255 laxness generally), project-LICHEN-worker6-0t11 (Rule 1/6 prefix divergence).
